place: One stroke of paper rubbed clean through night-black charcoal, the eraser's path forking and climbing to a bird cut white out of the dark.

source.model: authored by build agent (round 5, analyzer offline)

observations.what: Tall avian entity of calligraphic flame scrolls standing in profile-left
The reductive eraser marks: highlights cut cleanly into charcoal tone with a kneaded eraser to form the white beak, blank eye and white tendril rims

measured.role: Midtone atmospheric smoke and rubbed charcoal ground behind the creature
Light gray diffused background wash and middle-value forest canopy
Deep charcoal shading along the underbelly, root crevices, and shadow ribbons
Pale gray halo surrounding the crest and highlighting vertical tree barks

palette.notes: Lifted paper is a cold white with a blue lean, the surrounding charcoal a blue-black; kneaded-eraser putty adds a soft grey-blue so the island is two-tone with one mid value.

motifs.name: lift_putty
motifs.where: Lying at the stroke's edges where the kneaded eraser was pinched and set down.

shape.summary: A kneaded-eraser lump: soft grey-blue rounded putty stacked in two dough blocks with a pinched peak.

motifs.name: lift_crumb
motifs.where: Rolled off the eraser along the stroke.

shape.summary: Eraser crumbs: three or four rolled grey pellets curled on the paper, one flecked with black.

motifs.name: lift_rim
motifs.where: Flaring up at the stroke's turns like the white tendril rims around the bird's scrolls.

shape.summary: A white tendril rim: a tall flame-shaped white blade curling at the tip, with a black contour strip down one edge, on a black smear base.

motifs.name: lift_smear
motifs.where: At the stroke's tail where the eraser began and pushed the charcoal aside.

shape.summary: A charcoal smudge boulder: a soft blue-black rounded mound with one white erased streak across its top.

motifs.name: lift_cut_gate
motifs.where: Across the stroke two thirds of the way up.

shape.summary: Two paper-white blades with black contour edges, a white strip across their tops.

creatures.name: lift_white_bird
creatures.source: The bird's erased beak, blank eye and white tendril rims, taken as the whole figure
creatures.pose: A white cut-out of the bird, head bowed left, crest flaring up in white tendrils outlined in black, standing on a black smear.
creatures.why: The erased white is the drawing's sharpest mark; making the bird entirely of it gives the dark stroke a bright end.

legend.R: raised ground (plateau, one or more blocks above G)

focal.what: The white cut-out bird at the head of the stroke

composition.mass: The island is the erased stroke itself, a pale ribbon of lifted paper hanging in black; kneaded-eraser putty lumps and crumbs lie along it, white tendril rims flare up as beacons, and the bird is white, drawn by what was taken away.
composition.read: Up the length of the erased stroke from its southwest tail, one tier at a time, past smudge boulders and crumbs to where the stroke ends at the bird.

lighting.notes: cold desk lamp over black charcoal: Maximum black (#181818) is 12 percent of the drawing and holds every white cut; charcoal under cold light goes blue-black, and the erased paper reads bright against it.

rules: Everything walkable is lifted paper; charcoal only at the stroke's edges.
Tendril rims flare at the turns of the stroke.
Keep putty lumps off the centre line.

lens.differs: forest-medium used the eraser only for a few pale slabs in a dark basin; here the whole walkable world is the erasure, a single forked stroke over void, and the figure turns white while its surroundings go to blue-black.

shaper.name: ribbon
shaper.why: An eraser pass is one continuous stroke that lifts a strip of paper out of the tone; ribbon land over void is that strip, forking where the drawing's white tendril rims split.

surface_mix.why: Bands along the stroke: clean lifted paper (sand), a few grey crumb-strewn passes (stone) and the charcoal smear the eraser pushed to its edges (dirt).

cliff_treatment.why: The un-erased charcoal around the stroke: sheer blue-black walls under the pale surface.

figure_pose.why: The beak and eye in the drawing exist only as erased paper; this reading extends the erasure to the whole body, so the bird is the brightest thing in the dark.

concept.name: aspect-lift
concept.fragment: Round 5 reading authored by the build agent from pipeline/seed/analysis/forest.json and the drawing itself, without the analyzer (Gemini returns 402). One aspect of the charcoal drawing, "lift", becomes the place; the shaper, palette, lighting, props and the figure's pose are argued from that aspect alone. It must not repeat the round-4 forest readings (ash basin with soot trunks, taproot knoll with charred boles, birch spiral) or their shapers (basin, mound, spiral).
